question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $70u+31v=\text{gcd}(70,31).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}70 & = & 31\cdot 2 & + & 8 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 31 & = & 8\cdot 3 & + & 7 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 8 & = & 7\cdot 1 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(70,31)=1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8 & =70-31\cdot 2 \\ 7 & =31-8\cdot 3 \\ 1 & =8-7.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =8-7 \\  & =8-[31-8\cdot 3] \\  & =8\cdot 4-31 \\  & =[70-31\cdot 2]\cdot 4-31 \\  & =70\cdot 4-31\cdot 9 \\  & =70\cdot 4+31\cdot (-9)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=4$ and $v=-9.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=4+(-9)=-5.
$$
